items.title: Take-Two CEO Strauss Zelnick Won't Rule Out GTA 6 on Disc at Some Point, Insists Decision Had Nothing to Do With Concern Over Leaks
items.description: One of the big questions following the shock decision not to release GTA 6 on-disc at launch is whether Rockstar will ever release a disc version of the game. In a new interview with IGN, Strauss Zelnick, boss of Rockstar parent company Take-Two, refused to rule it out.
items.author: Wesley Yin-Poole
items.content:
One of the big questions following the shock decision not to release GTA 6 on-disc at launch is whether Rockstar will ever release a disc version of the game. In a new interview with IGN, Strauss Zelnick, boss of Rockstar parent company Take-Two, refused to rule it out.

Speaking today following the release of Take-Two’s Q1 2027 financials, Zelnick defended the company’s decision not to release GTA 6 on a disc, insisting when it comes to big games, discs “don’t really make sense for the consumer.”

And in a new interview with IGN, Zelnick doubled down on his comments to the investment community, confirming more than 90% of Take-Two’s sales are digital.

“In order to play video games, you need to be connected today,” Zelnick added. “So everyone's connected. So it's just a matter of the most efficient way to get the title into people's hands.”

That’s the situation for the launch of GTA 6, but what about the longer term view? We asked Zelnick if he could rule out the possibility of GTA 6 ever releasing on disc. Here's his response: “I wouldn't rule out anything at this stage of the game. What we've announced so far is what we're doing at the moment, but we are always open minded.”

After Rockstar confirmed the GTA 6 no disc situation back in June, some wondered if it was in part about preventing leaks in the run up to the game’s launch. Having no physical discs loaded with game data will help with "Rockstar's near-pathological secrecy," Rhys Elliot, head of market analysis at Alinea Analytics, told IGN at the time. It also ensured game data only unlocks at launch, meaning no damaging early leaks from copies "lost off the back of a truck." GTA 6 has already seen one major pre-launch leak, and with fans poring over every last snippet of information about the game, it's easy to see why Rockstar would want to keep control over every last detail.

However, speaking to IGN today, Zelnick denied security had anything to do with the decision. “No,” Zelnick responded when asked if concern over GTA 6 potentially leaking if it were released on disc factored into Take-Two’s thinking in any way.

There is an ongoing backlash not just to Rockstar’s decision on GTA 6, but also Sony’s announcement to discontinue PlayStation disc production from 2028. This has seen gamers continue to call on Sony to U-turn on its decision, signing online petitions and swarming over PlayStation social media posts to express concern about video game preservation and ownership — even overshadowing the release of new games that have nothing to do with what’s going on at Sony. Meanwhile, backers of physical media have called on gamers to boycott PlayStation for a week in August to send a message to Sony that its decision to kill discs from 2028 is unacceptable. Complaints have also come from other groups. The UK’s Digital Entertainment and Retail Association (ERA), for example, called Sony’s decision “a triumph of corporate convenience over consumer choice.”

Last week, Sony finally broke its silence on its decision to discontinue PlayStation discs to say it is not having any impact on its business now, and it doesn’t see any negative impact in the future. Executives have insisted Sony will not change its mind, while acknowledging “strong views” from the video game community.

And speaking to IGN, Zelnick offered a similar response to the backlash, expressing his belief that GTA 6 not releasing on a disc basically won’t hurt Take-Two financially. “I certainly hope there will be no negative impact and I don't expect that there will be one,” he said.

Zelnick agreed with the assertion that he sees a future when physical discs just go away completely (“yes, I do”), but didn’t want to put a timeframe on it. “I really wouldn't be able to guess,” he said. “And by going away, there'll still be some in the same way that there's still some vinyl in the recorded music business, but I don't believe it'll be a lot.”

And finally on the GTA 6 disc issue, Zelnick distanced Take-Two from the suggestion that it was influenced by Sony’s decision to discontinue PlayStation discs from 2028, stressing: “We wanted to do what was right for the project.”

When Sony announced its decision it said it was simply following consumer trends. “In response to shifting trends in consumer preference, new games will be released on PlayStation Store and at retailers in digital formats only,” Sid Shuman, Senior Director, Sony Interactive Entertainment Content Communications, said in a post on PlayStation Blog.

Sony's latest financials show an 82% digital download ratio for full game software across PS4 and PS5. Reinforcing this trend, Mat Piscatella, Senior Director and Video Game Industry Advisor at Circana, recently said that just seven PlayStation video games had sold more than 100,000 physical units so far this year in the U.S.. Only two PlayStation video games sold more than 10,000 physical units in the U.S. during the week ending July 11.

For Sony, going all-digital for new game releases will earn it more money from every sale at a time when console sales are expected to plummet due to their rising cost. For a first-party PlayStation game such as The Last of Us, Sony will only keep around 65% of the money from a physical copy, with around 30% going to the retailer and roughly another 5% on manufacturing costs. Meanwhile, for a physical copy of a third-party game such as the Activision-published Call of Duty, Sony will get a licensing fee, likely around 15%.

For downloads, however, the margins are much higher. For a first-party game sold via Sony's own PlayStation Store, the company obviously keeps 100% of the revenue. For third-party games such as Call of Duty, meanwhile, Sony keeps a 30% cut (so, roughly $21 for a $70 game).

We've got plenty more from Zelnick today, including his comments on the GTA 6 price points, and Netflix's timed exclusivity on the next GTA 6 trailer.

Photo by Steven Ferdman/Getty Images.

items.title: 'Pricing Has Not Kept Pace With Inflation' — Take-Two Boss Insists Rockstar Got GTA 6 Standard and Ultimate Edition Price Points Right
items.description: The standard edition of GTA 6 costs $80, which represents a $10 increase on the established price of a triple-A console game. That hike raised more than a few eyebrows when Rockstar launched GTA 6 preorders in June. So, what’s the thinking behind it? We asked Take-Two boss Strauss Zelnick in a new interview with IGN.
items.author: Wesley Yin-Poole
items.content:
The standard edition of GTA 6 costs $80, which represents a $10 increase on the established price of a triple-A console game. That hike raised more than a few eyebrows when Rockstar launched GTA 6 preorders in June. So, what’s the thinking behind it?

The Standard Edition of GTA 6 includes the base single-player experience, but the Ultimate Edition includes exclusive content, such as a mission and shops. The rights and wrongs of charging $20 extra for this content is already being heavily discussed by GTA 6 fans in a debate made all the more vociferous by Rockstar’s decision not to include a disc in the physical version.

In a new interview with IGN, Strauss Zelnick, boss of Rockstar parent company Take-Two, said the GTA 6 price was all about value.

“We aim always to deliver vastly more value than what we charge,” he said. “And we think that price point allows us to do just that. And then of course we have a premium opportunity for people who want to avail themselves of that. And even that one, again, we think is priced in a way so as to deliver much more value than what we're charging.”

Zelnick added that just because GTA 6 is $80, other games from Take-Two publishing labels won’t necessarily follow suit. “It's very much case by case,” he said, pointing to the $50 price point 2K went with for Mafia: The Old Country.

Earlier today, speaking in an investor-focused Q&A following Take-Two’s Q1 2027 financial results, Zelnick insisted video game pricing had not kept up with inflation.

“Look, I think that Rockstar got it right in terms of the pricing of this standard edition and the pricing of the deluxe edition,” he said. “And I think there's no doubt that consumers are really excited about both. And I think depending on your own ability to pay and how avid a consumer you are, you can choose between them. But the preorders have been exceptional and we're happy with the mix as well.

He added: “The truth is that the real cost of a AAA video game is a whole lot lower today than it was 20 years ago. Pricing has not kept pace with inflation. And our goal is to continue to over-deliver for our consumers, because how you feel about any experience is the intersection of the experience itself and what you pay for it. So to say that we expect that Grand Theft Auto 6 will be an incredible bargain as experiences go is a gross understatement, because Rockstar Games is known for over-delivering.”

“Our goal is not to maximize price,” Zelnick continued. “So in this case, I think what we've decided to do makes a whole lot of sense in the context of what we're delivering. And that's the lens through which we look going forward as well.”

In an IGN poll asking which edition of GTA 6 you’d buy, over 70% responded to say the $100 Ultimate Edition, which suggests Rockstar’s pricing strategy is working because it is convincing fans to spend that extra $20 for the exclusive content. This has led some to say that the Ultimate Edition is the default option for GTA 6, and the $80 version should be considered the cheaper option.

Also today, we have comments from Zelnick defending the decision not to release GTA 6 on a physical disc, as well as plans to release the next look at GTA 6 on Netflix.

Photo by Jakub Porzycki/NurPhoto via Getty Images.

items.title: Fortnite is Keeping Sprites for Next Season, a Gaming-Themed Crossover Expected to Feature Sonic, Persona and Tetris
items.description: Fortnite's popular Pokémon-like Sprites are sticking around for the game's next season — a gaming mash-up expected to feature Sonic the Hedgehog, Persona and Tetris.
items.author: Tom Phillips
items.content:
Fortnite's popular Pokémon-like Sprites are sticking around, developer Epic Games has confirmed, as it begins teasing a new gaming-themed season expected to feature crossovers with Sonic the Hedgehog, Persona and Tetris.

Sprites arrived in force at the beginning of Fortnite's current season, introducing a growing menagerie of cute creatures you collect, trade, and level up to increase their power. The addition has been hugely successful and created a community of Sprite-obsessed fans who have contributed to a notable boost in Fortnite's player count.

It's a welcome surprise, then, to see that Sprites are now confirmed as sticking around for next season — and a whole new generation of them are on the way. In a community blog, Epic Games has promised new powers, quality-of-life improvements based on player feedback, and "new ways to discover Sprites in (and out of) your games. Mysterious!

In a signal that Sprites are being treated as an important part of Fortnite going forward, Epic Games is launching a new Sprite Garden experience where collected Sprites can be showcased — both those from Season 3, and Gen 2 Sprites from Season 4. You'll even be able to visit friends' Sprite Gardens, too.

Season 4 will also finally see the addition of five community-designed Sprites, created as part of a player contest that saw more than 20,000 entries. These will include the Bullet Sprite (ammo boxes grant more ammo), Honey Sprite (sends a swarm of bees at enemies who attack you), Pond Sprite (increases swim speed and jump height) and X-Ray Sprite (reveals players through walls). My favorite, though, is the cute raccoon-like Dumpster Dive Sprite (gather loot from jumping into dumpsters).

Break the rules. Change the game.
8.20 pic.twitter.com/o8usTeRGsa

— Fortnite (@Fortnite) August 5, 2026

What else will next season bring? Sneaky dataminers have already spotted the suggestion of in-game posters expected to pop up across Fortnite's map later this month, teasing collaborations with Tetris, Sonic the Hedgehog, Pac-Man and Persona.

"Break the rules. Change the game," Epic has teased of Chapter 7 Season 4: Override, confirming its launch is set for August 20. Epic Games vice president Mark Rein has also now offered his customary teaser word for the incoming season: "Hackers."

Tom Phillips is IGN's News Editor. You can reach Tom at tom_phillips@ign.com or find him on Bluesky @tomphillipseg.bsky.social

items.title: LEGO Harry Potter Celebrates 25 Years With Ministry of Magic Set, and The First-Ever Minifigure of a Specific Character
items.description: LEGO will celebrate a quarter century of its Harry Potter range with the launch of a new Ministry of Magic set, featuring the first-ever Minifigure of Arabella Figg.
items.author: Tom Phillips
items.content:
LEGO will celebrate a quarter century of its Harry Potter range with the launch of a new Ministry of Magic set, featuring the first-ever Minifigure of Arabella Figg.

The 3,491-piece model will become available to LEGO Insiders on August 29, and gain a wider release on September 1 for the franchise's annual Back to Hogwarts Day.

The Ministry of Magic is a three-tiered set measuring 51cm (20 inches) tall, with a surface level that includes the Leaky Cauldron pub and the red telephone box used to access the Ministry's lower levels. The center portion of the build show the building's multi-story offices and a miniature version of its golden fountain. From the rear, features such as Umbridge's office and a Floo toilet can be seen. Finally, beneath all of this, the Hall of Prophecy lies in wait — including what looks to be the Ministry's magical Veil.

14 Minifigures are included in the set, including the aforementioned all-new Arabella Figg. Also on offer are: Ron Weasley, Hermione Granger, Harry Potter, Sirius Black, Kingsley Shacklebolt, Nymphadora Tonks, Arthur Weasley, Mad Eye Moody, Albus Dumbledore, Lucius Malfoy, Antonin Dolohov and Professor Umbridge. Shacklebolt's Lynx Patronus is also included.

LEGO first launched its Harry Potter range in 2021, the same year that the franchise's first film arrived in theaters. Over the past 25 years, more than 200 LEGO Harry Potter sets have been launched, with the largest being the 6,020-piece microscale Hogwarts Castle set launched in 2018.

The first LEGO Harry Potter set was the small Sorting Hat build, which featured a now rather dated minifigure of Harry Potter (featuring a yellow LEGO skin tone and full length legs). Fun fact: the Harry Potter range was the first to feature mini Minifigure legs (the non-bendable bottoms that are now used commonly for shorter or child minifigs).

Price-wise, The Ministry of Magic will set you back $449.99 / £389.99 / €429.99. As of yet, no Gift With Purchase has been announced. So, what do you think?

Tom Phillips is IGN's News Editor. You can reach Tom at tom_phillips@ign.com or find him on Bluesky @tomphillipseg.bsky.social

items.title: Rockstar Owner Take-Two Confirms GTA 6 Release Date Still on Track, Says 'GTA 6: An Extended Look' Will Help Grow 'Consumers' Passion and Anticipation'
items.description: Rockstar owner Take-Two has confirmed the current November 19 GTA 6 release date is still on track, and insisted the upcoming Grand Theft Auto VI: An Extended Look will help grow “consumers’ passion and anticipation" for the game.
items.author: Wesley Yin-Poole
items.content:
Rockstar owner Take-Two has confirmed the current November 19 GTA 6 release date is still on track, and insisted the upcoming Grand Theft Auto 6: An Extended Look will help grow “consumers’ passion and anticipation" for the game.

Reporting what it called “excellent” results for the first quarter of its 2027 financial year, Take-Two said the Grand Theft Auto series had “once again exceeded expectations,” with sales of GTA 5 over 230 million worldwide and 3% growth of the series overall in terms of microtransactions. GTA 5 is the second best-selling video game of all time, behind only Minecraft’s 400 million copies sold.

In its financial statement, Take-Two said “global excitement for the launch of Grand Theft Auto 6 continues to build, with the title having an exceptional start to preorders.” It did not put a number on those GTA 6 preorders or revenue generated from them, however recent analysis suggests GTA 6 generated approximately $180 million in digital preorders across the U.S. and the five biggest European markets during the last week of June (GTA 6 preorders went live at midnight, June 25). Net bookings for the quarter amounted to $1.39 billion, which was slightly above Take-Two's prediction of $1.32-$1.37 billion.

Take-Two did touch briefly on yesterday’s confirmation that the next official look at GTA 6 will come via what’s called the ‘Grand Theft Auto 6: An Extended Look,’ which will be exclusive to Netflix for six hours.

“With Rockstar Games’ recent announcement of Grand Theft Auto 6: An Extended Look coming on August 27th, we believe that consumers’ passion and anticipation for the next evolution of this iconic series will grow further leading up to the title’s November 19th release,” Take-Two said.

The other significant contribution to Take-Two’s Q1 financials was NBA 2K, which grew 7% in terms of Recurrent Consumer Spending (RCS) — in other words, microtransactions. NBA 2K26’s performance was “outstanding and concluded a record year for the franchise,” Take-Two added. To date, the title has sold-in over 12 million units, reflecting 9% growth compared to NBA 2K25.

“The achievements of this year’s iteration of the series are a testament to Visual Concepts’ ability continually to deliver new, innovative ways for fans to stay engaged, and our live-service execution remains a cornerstone of NBA 2K's sustained success,” Take-Two said. NBA 2K27 is due out this September.

Take-Two also mentioned 2K’s support of Borderlands 4, Sid Meier’s Civilization VII, and WWE 2K26 “with an array of new offerings, which enhanced player engagement and sentiment.” There are no firm numbers for these games.

Looking ahead, all eyes are on GTA 6, as you’d expect. Take-Two said it believes the current financial year will be an “inflection point” for the company, “one that will write an exciting new chapter in our history and provide the foundation for new levels of success and the creation of groundbreaking entertainment experiences.”

It reiterated its net bookings prediction for the year ($8-$8.2 billion), which represents approximately 20% growth over FY26 at the midpoint (GTA 6 will fuel most of that enormous growth). Take-Two said it expects revenue breakdown by its labels to be roughly 37% Rockstar Games, 34% Zynga, and 29% 2K. Other games without a release date include PGA Tour 2K27, WWE 2K27, Judas, Project Ethos, and the next BioShock.

Wesley is Director, News at IGN. Find him on Twitter at @wyp100. You can reach Wesley at wesley_yinpoole@ign.com or confidentially at wyp100@proton.me.

items.title: Nintendo Says Physical Games Still Account for 38.5% of Its Software Sales, Following Sony's Decision to Kill PS5 Discs
items.description: Boxed games still account for 38.5% of Nintendo's software sales, the Mario maker has said, suggesting it has no desire to kill physical media anytime soon.
items.author: Tom Phillips
items.content:
Boxed games still account for 38.5% of Nintendo's software sales, the Mario maker has said, suggesting that it has no desire to kill physical media anytime soon.

That comes in contrast to Sony, which recently raised eyebrows with its announcement that no new PlayStation 5 games would ship on disc from January 2028 onwards. While that change may still be 18 months away, new PS5 consoles and disc drive accessories are already being shipped with warning labels, cautioning consumers of the upcoming changes. The news also points to PlayStation 6 being an all-digital console too, it's believed.

As for Xbox, while it isn't abandoning discs entirely anytime soon, the company is reportedly developing a system of transferring game licenses from physical game discs to digital ownership.

Nintendo still enjoys a strong physical game presence, however — even if this is shrinking. In its latest financial results, Nintendo stated that its ratio of physical game sales to digital had shrunk by 2.2 points, meaning 61.5% of its games sold are now digital downloads, while 38.5% are still sold in a box.

While this percentage is growing smaller, it remains a hefty proportion — and something that sees Nintendo differ signficantly from other publishers. Only yesterday, Capcom stated that "approximately 90%" of its game sales were now digital. But the difference here makes some sense, considering the fact that Nintendo's vast audience caters to many younger and more casual players.

This audience is more likely to buy physical games (or have them bought for them) to share among family members, or to eventually resell to take advantage of their trade-in value. Nintendo also has numerous die-hard fans, who may alternatively wish to keep their physical games as part of a larger collection.

With Switch 2 only launched last year, it seems unlikely that Nintendo will make any changes to physical game availability anytime soon, even as manufacturing and shipping increase. Instead, Nintendo has adopted something of a hybrid approach, with physical games being released on a mix of regular cartridges, cheaper Game-Key Cards, as well as digital codes in a box (which is how the Switch 2 port of Diablo 4 will reportedly arrive).

How long Nintendo will keep its sizable physical games presence over the coming generation will be interesting to see. While the company will likely make no rash decisions, it has recently begun incentivizing digital purchases for new Switch 2 games by making them around $10 cheaper than their boxed counterparts.

Upcoming Switch 2 game launches include Fire Emblem: Fortune's Weave on September 17, Switch Sports Resort on October 22, and the new Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake before the end of this year. 2027 titles already announced include Xenoblade Genesis, plus Pokémon Winds and Pokémon Waves.

items.title: Target is Slicing Open Pokémon Card Boxes Before They're Sold in a Bid to Deter Scalpers, Fans Say
items.description: Target is reportedly cutting the shrink wrap on boxes of new Pokémon cards to deter scalpers, who buy stock in bulk simply for the resale market.
items.author: Tom Phillips
items.content:
Target is reportedly cutting the shrink wrap on boxes of new Pokémon cards to deter scalpers in some stores, who buy stock in bulk simply for the resale market.

That's according to fans who report seeing some Target employees fully removing the plastic wrap from boxes of cards in stores, and receiving cut-open card boxes when ordering online.

While Target is yet to officially comment on the practice, fans strongly believe this is a tactic to put off scalpers, who purchase the lucrative cards only to sell them on for a profit.

Card boxes that have their packaging removed make no difference to actual collectors, but are worth far less when sold second-hand — as there would be no way of proving the cards inside haven't already been opened, and had their rarest pulls removed.

Didn’t realise Target was also cutting the shrink wrap for online orders aswell! 👀✂️ https://t.co/KaNC24onqE pic.twitter.com/JnTLlJpMEw

— Pokemon Giveaways (@PokeTCGiveaways) August 6, 2026

A Target employee was cutting the shrink wrap on sealed Pokémon products (Prismatic Evolutions ETBs in the video) and stated that it's a directive from Corporate to prevent scalpers from purchasing products solely to flip. How do you all feel about this? Target W or Target L? 🎯… pic.twitter.com/5ToUCHQINn

— Pokemon Alerts & News (@PokeTCGAlerts) June 2, 2026

Response to the practice has been mostly positive, with praise from fans who have struggled to buy cards due to their increasing scarcity.

"Good, tired of scalpers ruining everything," one fan wrote on social media. "I hope target keeps doing this."

"Anything that stops the scalpers is fine with me," said another. "All the people complaining can go buy their Pokémon cards somewhere else. Target will still sell out. I wish everyone did it."

"I 100% agree with this until the scalping situation is solved," said a third. "Usually the only ones that care about box condition are resellers 🤣 you could throw my box across the store as long as the cards are ok."

But not everyone is on board. Some fans say the practice risks damaging the stock, while others say that it will only make sealed boxes even more expensive — playing into the hands of the scalpers further.

Pokémon cards have become a prime target for scalpers and thieves over the past few years due to their soaring popularity and the perceived value of rare cards. New card releases frequently sell out completely, and The Pokémon Company has appeared unable or unwilling to fully keep up with demand — despite a staggering 10 billion cards printed last year alone.

Yesterday, we reported that The Pokémon Center store in Japan is now limiting purchases only to Japanese citizens, following the introduction of facial recognition for adults and children in some stores. High demand for cards has also led to numerous incidents of thefts and violence between shoppers, and
barely a month goes by without a report of a trading card store being robbed. Meanwhile, one desperate Pokémon fan was recently arrested in Pasadena, California, after hiding inside a closed Best Buy ahead of a Pokémon card drop.

Image credit: Martin Lelievre / AFP via Getty Images

items.title: Layoffs Hit Staff at Crossfire Developer That’s No Moon
items.description: In yet another sweep of layoffs within the gaming space, Crossfire developer That’s No Moon has axed an as-yet undetermined number of staff.
items.author: Virginia Glaze
items.content:
In yet another sweep of layoffs within the gaming space, Crossfire developer That’s No Moon has axed an as-yet undetermined number of staff.

Now-former employees began posting about the situation on their LinkedIn profiles on August 6, confirming that they were affected by layoffs at the studio. Roles impacted appear to have included technical and environmental artists. IGN has reached out to That's No Moon for comment.

That’s No Moon was founded in 2021 by industry vets from powerhouse developers like Naughty Dog and Infinity Ward. Based in Los Angeles, it revealed its first AAA offering, a narrative-driven, single-player title called Crossfire, at Summer Game Fest 2026.

Thus far, the project doesn't have an official release date, but the minds behind the game gave players a first look at what they can expect duing an in-depth showcase, which they presented alongside Geoff Keighley at Summer Game Fest. Crossfire features a unique mechanic called 'adaptive cover,' where characters dynamically adapt their stances in reaction to terrain and nearby enemies.

Game director Jacob Minkoff explained that it rewards tactical thinking, stealth, and repositioning, saying it "fundamentally changes your relationship with the environment and becomes an active skill to master" while playing.

Crossfire follows the journeys of enemy operators Layla Qassem and Delroy Cross as they fight for survival in a tenuous, but temorary, alliance. Layla's story begins during a routine reconnaissance mission in the Atlas Mountains that turns into a "harrowing struggle" in which she must confront her "rigid worldview." Cross, described as a "tier one operator and elite member" of Global Risk, is forced to confront his own beliefs during a mission for Sodara Biotech.

As you can probably guess, Crossfire takes place in the world of the multiplayer shooter of the same name, though it hones in on two members of these opposing factions for a focused storyline that forces enemies into a union of sorts.

Crossfire is in development for PC, PlayStation 5, and Xbox Series X, and is currently available to wishlist on Steam, the PlayStation store, and the Microsoft store.

These are the latest layoffs to impact a major gaming studio after Psychonauts developer Double Fine laid off a quarter of its staff following its return to independent ownership last month as a result of Xbox's massive restructuring efforts.

items.title: American Squid Game Spinoff Series Reportedly Canceled at Netflix
items.description: Netflix has reportedly chosen to shelve David Fincher’s American Squid Game spinoff series, according to sources close to the project.
items.author: Virginia Glaze
items.content:
Netflix has reportedly chosen to shelve David Fincher’s American Squid Game spinoff series, according to sources close to the project.

Reports of the spinoff first surfaced in 2024, and it’s been slow going ever since then. Dennis Kenny, creator of the 2013 British thriller series Utopia, was attached to write the script, with Fincher set to direct.

However, nothing moved forward for months — at least, not publicly. Then, in November 2025, the show was listed on the Film and Television Industry Alliance website with the title ‘Squid Game: America.’ The site listed a shoot date for February 2026 in Los Angeles, but given this most recent information, it’s safe to say this is no longer the case.

Sources informed The Playlist about the spinoff’s cancellation, telling the outlet that Netflix’s goals for the franchise have substantially changed since Fincher’s version was first conceptualized. Insiders suggested that Netflix was initially eager for an American take on their record-breaking Korean series, but are now focused on exploring stories within the Squid Game universe in “individual international markets” — though whether that means country-specific spinoffs (such as Squid Game: Brazil, Norway, etc.) remains unclear.

The Playlist’s sources reportedly “stressed” that such regional versions of the show are not known to be in the development, though Fincher’s Squid Game: America seems to firmly be a thing of the past. As for why this happened, sources gave a few reasons, pointing to a long production process, changes at the executive level within Netflix, and Fincher taking on other projects like his film The Adventures of Cliff Booth.

This makes Cate Blanchett’s surprise appearance at the end of Season 3 even more confusing, though it was confirmed that her involvement in the show wasn’t tied to Fincher’s series. It did directly hint that there were more versions of the Games out there in the world, and set up a future follow-up exploring players and the VIPs in other countries.

Squid Game’s original creator, Hwang Dong-hyuk, previously bandied about the idea of a spinoff series exploring what happens to its characters in the time skip between seasons one and two. However, he also confirmed that Season 3 was the end-all, be-all finale of the entire story, saying, "It's the finale for the whole series. The whole show. It's time to say goodbye."

For now, it’s anyone’s guess as to what Netflix has planned for Squid Game as an IP, but those itching for more Korean thrillers on the streamer should turn their eyes to Mask Girl, another dark, time-jumping series that hits many of the same tonal notes (minus the deadly childrens' games).

IGN has reached out to Netflix for comment.

items.title: Quake Gets Free New Campaign Co-Developed by MachineGames for Game's 30th Anniversary
items.description: The 2021 remaster of Quake has gotten a new 19-level campaign co-developed by MachineGames in honor of the FPS' 30th anniversary.
items.author: Cade Onder
items.content:
The 2021 remaster of Quake has gotten a new, 19-level campaign co-developed by MachineGames in honor of the FPS' 30th anniversary.

At QuakeCon, id Software and MachineGames announced a free new campaign for the 2021 version of Quake. The new campaign is titled Dawn of the Machine and is available for Quake owners right now at no extra cost. Ranger is stuck in a time loop and must solve puzzles and fight new foes using new weapons (including an axe!) to survive. It includes a new soundtrack, new deathmatch maps, and achievements.

id Software and MachineGames have also ensured there will be a high degree of replayability with these levels, noting that the narrative presentation of the time loop allows for players to tackle them to their hearts' content and make new discoveries. If you load up a level again, new paths will unlock, new secrets will be made available, and there will be new upgrades for you to grow stronger. Ultimately, it sounds like a lot of really exciting content made available to all players through a free update.

MachineGames wears its Quake influences on its sleeve with its games, as the studio is widely regarded as one of the best FPS developers in the industry right now. They made a name for themselves on the recent Wolfenstein games, and it's expected that they will complete their Wolfenstein trilogy in the future, but nothing has been formally announced on that particular front.

The team also cut its teeth on Indiana Jones and the Great Circle, an immersive first-person adventure game that shies away from over-the-top gunplay. Their experience with both franchises makes them a great fit for this new Quake campaign, as they've proven their mettle at both FPS combat and making thoughtful and fun puzzles.

items.title: Call of Duty: World at War Multiplayer Nearly Had a Much Larger Focus on Vehicles
items.description: Dataminers have discovered content that suggests Call of Duty: World at War would've had a much larger focus on vehicle combat in its multiplayer.
items.author: Cade Onder
items.content:
Dataminers have discovered content that suggests Call of Duty: World at War would've had a much larger focus on vehicle combat in its multiplayer modes.

Back in the mid to late 2000s, Call of Duty was defining its formula. It became annualized, with multiple studios alternating between games, ast-paced and class-based PvP multiplayer modes, and a blockbuster campaign. Still, there was a lot to figure out on what exactly those multiplayer experiences would look like. We know it well now, but it seems that Treyarch was playing around with vehicles in the series' earliest multiplayer modes.

Call of Duty 3 and Call of Duty: World at War's multiplayer modes both featured vehicles that players could freely get into and use. In World at War, it felt like a bit of an afterthought, as only four maps actually had tanks, but it turns out there were much larger plans for them.

As discovered by ForwardLeaks and @TheSpoopatron on X, World at War would've allowed players to call in tanks after obtaining seven kills. These tanks would've been fully customizable with special perks, different weapons, and more. Players would've been able to equip flamethrowers to the tanks, have control over their speed, and much more.

To support all of this, World at War would have had more maps that were specifically designed to accommodate tanks. Unfortunately, all of this got cut (or at least drastically reduced) before launch. It's unclear why Treyarch pulled back on this, but it's possible that it wasn't as fun or didn't work as well as they'd hoped.

World at War also suffered from a fairly rushed development. Despite having a two-year dev cycle, the game underwent massive revisions and changes, which may be another reason why these features and maps were cut.

After a play reached a 7 kill streak, the player would have the ability to call in a tank. The tank would be able to be fully… pic.twitter.com/6zzWJ6vl9d

— Forward (@ForwardLeaks) August 6, 2026

• Railway (mp_railway)
• Sandtrap (mp_sandtrap)
• Village (mp_village)
• Zoo (mp_zoo)

* indicates map released in WaW pic.twitter.com/hU6jd95Jzi

— Forward (@ForwardLeaks) August 6, 2026

It's interesting to think about what Call of Duty might have looked like, had these features shipped. Would vehicles have played a bigger part in future Call of Duty games? It's hard to say. The recent Modern Warfare games have had vehicles as part of its Ground War mode, seemingly as a way to compete with large-scale multiplayer games like Battlefield. It's a fun addition, but it has yet to rival the more intense 6v6 experiences in the game.

Players also discovered a cut Zombies tower defense mode in the recent Black Ops ports. Those ports are among the best selling games of 2026, as fans have flocked to the older games in droves.

items.title: Jurassic World Rebirth Director Exits Film Over 'Creative Differences'
items.description: Gareth Edwards has exited the Jurassic World Rebirth sequel as its director, citing “creative differences” as the reason for his departure from the project.
items.author: Virginia Glaze
items.content:
Gareth Edwards has exited the Jurassic World Rebirth sequel as its director, citing “creative differences” as the reason for his departure from the project.

Sources informed The Hollywood Reporter of his exit, with Universal Studios providing a succinct statement on the matter. “We had an incredible experience working with Gareth on Jurassic World Rebirth,” they told the outlet.

While it’s as-yet unclear who will direct the project now, this bump in the road isn’t the end for Rebirth’s sequel. A script has already been penned by David Koepp, who famously wrote the script for the original Jurassic Park film in 1993 and 1997’s The Lost World: Jurassic Park.

Rebirth’s stars Scarlett Johansson, Mahershala Ali, and Jonathan Bailey are also expected to return, though nothing has been confirmed as of yet, since schedules are reportedly still being worked out. The film famously made Johansson the highest-grossing lead actor ever, launching her over Robert Downey Jr. and Samuel L. Jackson.

It was a hugely profitable flick, grossing over $750 million at the box office, in part due to its massive opening weekend, where it raked up $300 million globally. While the numbers speak for themselves, critics’ opinions were decidedly less positive, with IGN’s Clint Gage rating Rebirth a 5 out of 10, arguing the film “plays it frustratingly safe, falling back on the blueprint of the original film, but not shedding any of the problems with the more recent movies.”

Rebirth was a fairly stand-alone experience, though its ending certainly pointed to a continuation of its story, which took place in the aftermath of the events of Jurassic World Dominion. For now, Universal seems to be moving full-speed ahead as fans await more details.

items.title: Sam Neill to Play Role in Sony Pictures' Legend of Zelda Movie, Dichen Lachman and Yvonne Strahovski Also Confirmed
items.description: The late great Sam Neill will reportedly make a posthumous appearance in Sony Pictures’ forthcoming Legend of Zelda film, with Dichen Lachman and Yvonne Strahovski also confirmed to star.
items.author: Virginia Glaze
items.content:
The late great Sam Neill will reportedly make a posthumous appearance in Sony Pictures’ forthcoming Legend of Zelda film, with Dichen Lachman and Yvonne Strahovski also confirmed to star.

Sources alerted Deadline of the news, which the outlet published on August 6 — the same day that Uli Latukefu was revealed to play the beloved game series’ big bad, Ganondorf.

Thus far, nothing is known about what role Neill will play in the movie, and neither Sony nor Neill’s team could be reached for comment. Both Sony and Nintendo have been tight-lipped regarding news about the project, but there are a few things we do know thus far.

Benjamin Evan Ainsworth is set to play Link, as officially revealed by Nintendo in November 2025, while Bo Bragason will take on the role of Princess Zelda. Footage from the movie’s set also leaked online around this time, showing an actor who appears to be Dichen Lachman playing Impa. Deadline is now able to confirm that she is, indeed, protraying Impa in the film, with Yvonne Strahovski also confirmed to play a "queen" character, though nothing else about her role was shared.

Sam Neill died on July 13, 2026 in Sydney, Australia at 78 years old. The prolific actor is best known for his performance as Dr. Alan Grant in three Jurassic Park movies, as well as Chester Campbell in the historical drama series Peaky Blinders.

Neill’s death was described as “sudden and unexpected” in a statement shared to his official Instagram account at the time, which confirmed that he “surrounded by family and passed with the dignity that has characterised his whole life.”

Neill is one of the better-known stars involved in the Legend of Zelda movie, with Aisnworth and Bragason being relatively fresh faces. Australian actor Uli Latukefu has appeared in a fair few big productions, best known for playing a young Dwayne Johnson in the NBC comedy Young Rock and Byamba in Netflix’s Marco Polo series.

Bragason notably starred in BBC One’s Three Girls drama series and historical fantasy romp Renegade Nell on Disney+. You’ve probably seen Ainsworth in the latest season of House of the Dragon, where he shines as Prince Daeron Targaryen, a young prince trapped between a rock and a hard place, to say the least.

The Legend of Zelda is scheduled to hit theaters on April 30, 2027. For now, fans can look forward to the Ocarina of Time remake, which fans believe will release in November this year in direct competition with the highly-anticipated GTA 6.

items.title: Hideki Kamiya Reveals Spider-Man 2 Scene That Inspired Key Game Sequence in Okami
items.description: Hideki Kamiya revealed that Okami's main planner took inspiration from a scene in Sam Raimi’s Spider-Man 2 movie to shape one particular moment in the highly-acclaimed 2006 game.
items.author: Virginia Glaze
items.content:
Hideki Kamiya revealed that Okami's main planner took inspiration from a scene in Sam Raimi’s Spider-Man 2 movie to shape one particular moment in the highly-acclaimed 2006 game.

If you’ve seen the movie and played Okami, you probably know what moment I’m talking about. If you haven’t, this is your warning that spoilers lie ahead (though, to be fair, both of these things are over 20 years old at this point).

In the unlikely event you haven’t seen the Tobey Maguire Spider-Man movies, there’s a scene in the second film where he uses his webs to stop a runaway train at the last second. It’s an iconic moment that has sparked endless tributes and parodies over the years — and it apparently inspired a story beat in Okami, of all things.

In the game, players must find a way to cross a massive, raging river in order to progress to another area. A non-playable character is tasked with repairing the bridge that crosses this river, but in the middle of his chore, a log comes flying downstream at top speeds, prompting a timed gameplay segment where Amaterasu is tasked with slowing the log down using her Vine power before she careens off the side of a waterfall.

As told by Okami director Hideki Kamiya on his official X/Twitter account, this segment was created by planner Hiroshi Shibata, who took direct inspiration from Spider-Man 2.

“This scene was planned by Shibata-san, who served as the main planner, drawing inspiration from the train scene in Sam Raimi's Spider-Man 2,” Kamiya said matter-of-factly in response to a clip from the moment posted to the official Okami X account.

この場面は、メインプランナーを務めてくれた柴田さんが、サム・ライミ版スパイダーマン2の電車の場面から着想を得て企画しました… https://t.co/O9ZtBYNlLZ

— 神谷英樹🍀 Hideki Kamiya🍀 (@HidekiKamiya_X) August 5, 2026

This is one of several insights that Kamiya has given about his games over the last few months, most recently confirming that Leon S. Kennedy was, indeed, named after the 1994 movie Leon: The Professional. Kamiya famously directed Resident Evil 2, creating one of the series’ most iconic characters whose popularity has stood the test of time. (He’s even getting a life-sized statue in Shibuya later this year to celebrate Resident Evil’s 30th anniversary.)

Okami is finally getting a sequel game, produced by the newly-formed Clovers, founded by Kamiya after his exit from Platinum Games. In collaboration with Capcom, it is a direct continuation of Okami’s main story, not a spin-off in the vein of Okamiden on the DS.

“I always wanted to create an Ōkami sequel,” Kamiya told us in an exclusive interview in February 2025. “Thinking back to about 19 years ago when I first created the game, you have to remember that the story itself isn't really complete, and I always wanted to complete this game.”

For now, not much else is known about the project, with Clovers saying it will be some time before anything further is shown off publicly. However, we do know that it's being developed in Capcom's RE engine, which gives us a vague idea of what the sequel's visual design might look like off the back of its unique art style in the original game.

items.title: The Legend of Zelda Movie Casts Uli Latukefu as Ganondorf
items.description: The Legend of Zelda movie has revealed who will be playing Ganondorf.
items.author: Cade Onder
items.content:
The Legend of Zelda movie has found its Ganondorf.

According to a report from Deadline, Uli Latukefu will play the film's villain, Ganondorf. The actor also reportedly signed a multi-picture deal, meaning the studio will have the opportunity to bring him back for sequels, should the film be a success.

The Legend of Zelda film wrapped filming earlier this year, and somehow, Sony and Nintendo have managed to keep a tight lid on everything in the movie. The only other confirmed castings are for Link and Zelda, who are already relatively unknown actors. A handful of images also trickled out, but they don't reveal much about the movie. Ultimately, we don't know much about the film, and it's less than a year away from release.

We're not even sure if Ganondorf will be physically played by Latukefu. Ganondorf may be a CG creature, and that's why they were able to keep this casting under wraps for so long. If he's just providing the voice, the studio may have been able to avoid any leaks for a while. We'll likely find out sometime later this year, as Nintendo will presumably drop the first trailer before the holiday season.

This will be Nintendo's second attempt at a modern big-screen adaptation of one of its franchises. Mario graced the screens in an animated film in 2023 and returned in a sequel earlier this year. Although the films aren't critical darlings, they make heaps of money at the box office and largely capture the spirit of the games in a way that the 90s Mario movie didn't. This will be the first attempt at bringing Zelda to the big screen, and it remains to be seen if Nintendo will be able to replicate the success of Mario with this franchise.

The Legend of Zelda movie hits theaters on April 30, 2027.

items.title: Sony Is Forcing PSSR 2.0 in Latest PS5 Pro Beta
items.author: Jacqueline Thomas
items.content:
Back when the PS5 Pro came out, PSSR, or PlayStation Spectral Super Resolution was one of its biggest selling points. It didn't have the best start, but Sony released PSSR 2 back in March, with much better visual quality. And now, it seems that future updates will have the refreshed upscaler enabled by default.

According to a post on ResetEra – so obviously take this with a grain of salt – the latest PS5 Pro beta system update has PSSR 2 enabled by default. The option to enable or disable the new upscaler has been around for a while, hidden in the video output settings, where you'd find a toggle to "enhance PSSR image quality." The main difference with this beta update is that toggle is now enabled by default, rather than needing the user to turn in it on in the current retail system software.

The whole reason this toggle exists is to essentially force the new upscaling model in games that haven't been updated with it. While some folks might not love the fact that Sony is forcing a system setting on, there's not really much reason to not use PSSR 2.0 over the launch PSSR. When you go into the settings to enable PSSR 2, there is a tooltip that tells you to disable if you "experience unexpected behavior during gameplay" – essentially visual artifacts and glitches.

But in the four-ish months since PSSR 2.0 rolled out, I've had it enabled and haven't noticed any weird visual glitches. Apparently Sony also hasn't seen many issues, otherwise it wouldn't be forcing it on by default. Even though this feature will probably be enabled by default on the stable system software, you will still be able to go in to Settings, then Screen and Video, then Video Output and disable Enhance PSSR Image Quality. Though, you should probably only disable it if you're running into problems on your PS5 Pro.

As for when this will make its way to the retail build of the PS5 Pro's system software, it's anyone's guess. But in the meantime, you can just go in and enable it on your PS5 Pro and enjoy the better visual quality in any game that uses PSSR.

items.title: Three First Print Copies of Pokemon Red, Blue, and Yellow Sell for $2 Million in Second-Largest Video Game Transaction Ever
items.description: Three first print Pokemon games are selling for an eye-watering $2 million to the owner of the Dubai Collection, one of the most prominent and highly-graded collections of video games and trading cards in the world.
items.author: Virginia Glaze
items.content:
Three first print Pokemon games are selling for an eye-watering $2 million to the owner of the Dubai Collection, one of the most prominent and highly-graded collections of video games and trading cards in the world.

The games in question are three first print copies of the original Pokemon titles for the Game Boy: Pokemon Blue Version, Pokemon Red Version, and Pokemon Yellow Version: Special Pikachu Edition. These were some of the earliest-manufactured copies for the series, and the original seals on all three were completely intact. Each copy was graded and encapsulated by PSA, one of the most prominent third-party grading agencies in the business, which gave them equally jaw-dropping scores: 9.8 (Blue), 10 (Red), and 10 (Yellow), making them the world's highest-graded first print collection among first print Pokemon games.

Nathan Howerton, owner and founder of Nostalgix, a private collectibles brokerage service that facilitated the transaction, spoke with IGN about the significance of the sale and what it means for physical games in an industry that’s hurtling toward a digital future.

"In an increasingly digital world, collectors continue to place extraordinary value on physical media,” he told us. “The sale of these three PSA-graded Pokémon games shows that truly exceptional physical copies aren't just nostalgic artifacts — they're irreplaceable pieces of gaming history.”

Howerton told us that this deal marks the second-largest graded video game transaction ever completed, only behind a copy of Super Mario Bros. for the NES that sold at auction for $3 million back in June. This copy was given a 9.6 by PSA, a score that would later be eclipsed by 97 pristine, never-before-seen versions of Super Mario Bros. / Duck Hunt that were discovered in a Wisconsin warehouse not long afterward, five of which were given 10s in a historic first for the agency.

As told in a previous interview with IGN, PSA very rarely gives out 10s for video games. The fact that three copies of the original Pokemon games — some of the most impactful titles in video game history — were graded so highly speaks to their pristine condition, meaning that the company could barely find anything, if at all, that was flawed about them.

“We look at so many things, and everything has at least some flaws,” Claire Shelton, Head of PSA Video Games, told us in July. “We’re looking for perfection, or at least as close to it as you can come. Because with injection-molded parts, there’s always going to be pulloff lines right from where something is detached from a mold, or just the intricacies of manufacturing are going to leave things with a little bit of inconsistency.”

Howerton says this landmark $2 million sale signals an evolution in the collectibles marketplace, elevating games to a point where “the rarest physical games are now being viewed alongside the world's most significant collectibles."

"A $2 million transaction for three graded Pokémon games would have seemed unimaginable a decade ago. Today, it reflects the growing recognition that historically important, investment-grade games deserve to be mentioned alongside the most valuable comics, trading cards, and sports memorabilia in the world," he said.

His remarks regarding physical media in a progressively digital landscape aren’t off the mark; given players' heated response toward Sony’s divisive decision to stop printing physical games as of January 2028, it’s clear that gamers value their tangible titles — enough to spend $2 million on them.

Virginia (she/her) is IGN’s News Editor. With ten years of experience reporting on games and entertainment, she’s got a storied background in the fighting game community, influencer news, and viral online trends. Find her on Twitter at @TheeMissGlaze.

items.title: 'This Is Unbelievably Scummy' - GTA 6 Fans Are Annoyed By Netflix's Paywalled Extended Look at the Game
items.description: Grand Theft Auto 6 fans aren't thrilled with Rockstar's decision to release the next look at the game through Netflix.
items.author: Cade Onder
items.content:
Grand Theft Auto 6 fans aren't thrilled with Rockstar's decision to release the next look at the game through Netflix.

Earlier today, Rockstar Games confirmed it will debut an "extended look" at Grand Theft Auto 6 on August 27 at 3pm ET through Netflix. The extended look will also be available at 9pm ET on YouTube, but for six hours, it will essentially be paywalled behind a Netflix subscription. Essentially, Rockstar and Netflix are asking fans to fork over some cash to see the game's next big marketing beat the moment it goes live. Given the high anticipation for this game, there'll certainly be people who sign up for Netflix just to watch this instead of waiting for it to release for free on YouTube later that evening.

As you might imagine, some fans find the entire thing a bit odd and are even upset about the move.

"This is unbelievably scummy," said one fan on X. "Everyone is excited for the extended look of GTA 6, but it's premiering on Netflix first, which will influence people to get a subscription. This needs to be called out, because if any other studio, such as Bethesda, did this, they would be crucified."

"Hiding the first potential gameplay reveal behind a subscription, even if cheap and temporary, is peak Rockstar arrogance," said another.

There are numerous other near-identical messages under Rockstar's social media posts about the announcement, so these aren't isolated comments. Some have questioned why Netflix was even chosen for this event. It's likely Rockstar and Netflix partnered up after the streamer helped release Red Dead Redemption and the remastered GTA trilogy through its service, making the games accessible to millions of people who may not own a console or PC.

There are also fears that Netflix might not be able to handle the demand for the new look at GTA 6. The service is pretty notorious for crashing under pressure, particularly when there's a highly anticipated premiere of a new show like Stranger Things or a live sporting event. Is Netflix prepared to handle millions of people flooding its servers at once to catch a glimpse at GTA 6? We can only hope.

As of right now, we're not quite sure what will be featured in this new look. Will it be raw gameplay? A playthrough of a mission? A very long trailer? Some are hoping that we'll get 15–30 minutes of footage of the game, which seems reasonable for something that is premiering on Netflix. Rockstar released 10 minutes of gameplay for Red Dead Redemption 2 ahead of its release across two gameplay deep dive videos, so an even deeper look at GTA 6 doesn't feel totally out of the question.

The entire situation has resulted in a second wave of backlash against GTA 6. Although Rockstar is treating the game like an unprecedented event, some fans aren't happy about the ways the company is going about it. In June, Rockstar confirmed that GTA 6 will not release on a disc, saying physical copies would only include a digital code. It's speculated that Rockstar is doing this to prevent the game from leaking through early copies, but physical media fans are frustrated about the game from a preservation perspective. On top of that, the game is also $80 and certain content is locked behind a $100 ultimate edition.

Whether or not any of these annoyances are enough to turn people off to the game remains to be seen. GTA 6 is expected to be a pop culture golliath either way, and will likely be one of the biggest entertainment releases in history.

Cade Onder is a freelancer for IGN's news team. He covers all things entertainment, including gaming, film, and more. You can find him on Twitter @Cade_Onder.

items.title: The Warrior Cats Books are Finally Getting a Major Video Game Adaptation
items.description: Erin Hunter’s iconic young adult book series, Warriors, is finally getting its first major video game, and it’s a turn-based RPG.
items.author: Virginia Glaze
items.content:
Erin Hunter’s iconic young adult book series, Warriors, is finally getting its first major video game, and it’s a turn-based RPG.

If you grew up with Firestar and the Four Clans, you’ve been waiting since 2003 for there to be some whisper of a large-scale, official adaptation following his journey from kittypet to Clan Leader. While comic books chronicling the Clans’ brutal and dramatic histories have been around since the mid-2000s, news of a film, series, or full-scale video game has been disappointing at best, leaving fans to create their own animations in labors of love that stand as a testament to how well-loved the franchise has been for the last two decades (we'll never forget you, SSSWarriorCats).

That all changed in 2026 — 23 years after the first book was published — when, finally, it was revealed that the Warriors series is getting both an animated show on Disney+ and its own officially licensed video game released on consoles and Steam.

A trailer shared to the official Warrior Cats Instagram account on August 5 gave fans a first look at the game, titled Warrior Cats: Clans of the Forest. It’s a turn-based RPG coming to PC (Steam), PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X and S, Nintendo Switch, and Nintendo Switch 2 this fall.

Players will create their own cat, choose a clan, and embark on an original adventure through the plains, forests, rivers, and swamps that generations of readers have come to know and love over the years. The trailer showcased a glimpse at what combat will look like, with players and members of their chosen Clan facing off against snakes, badgers, and even dogs. Traversal also looks as immersive as one would expect for such a game, allowing players to climb up trees and race through the wilderness to catch prey and explore their surroundings.

They’ll even get to meet iconic characters from the books, with the trailer specifically showing off the beautiful but scarred Brightheart and what seems to be Cloudtail, Firestar’s nephew. Thus far, it’s unclear if players will be able to choose specific roles, leaving the option of being a Medicine Cat up in the air for now.

Warrior Cats: Clans of the Forest is developed by TRAILMARK Games, an IP-focused developer based out of Minnesota best known for titles like Cruis’n Blast, Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles Arcade: Wrath of the Mutants, and The Walking Dead: Streets of Survival. It’s got a solid track record, and we can’t wait to see how Clans of the Forest shapes up by launch in just a few more months.

While Clans of the Forest is technically the first full-scale Warriors game published on major consoles and Steam, it isn’t the first officially licensed one; Warrior Cats: Ultimate Edition, an RPG that similarly lets players create their own cat within the world of the books, was released on Roblox in 2021. Developed by Aldrich-Callen Studios and Coolabi Group (who now owns the rights to the Warrior Cats IP), it was initially released in 2019 with limited features, and an expansion titled Warrior Cats: Lake Territory is currently in development. (A mobile game is also in the works, slated for release in 2027, though not much is known about the title at present.)

This is the latest big news for Warriors fans after Disney confirmed that an animated series adapting the beloved novels is in active production. Revealed in June, CG studio Original Force (God of War 2018, Black Myth: Wukong) is animating the show on behalf of Tencent Video and Coolabi, with A.C. Bradley (Ms Marvel, What If?) listed as showrunner. Rodrigo Blaas (Finding Nemo, The Incredibles, Wall-E) is set to direct in collaboration with independent animation studio El Guiri Studios (Star Wars Visions: Sith).

Concept art for the show was revealed in July, showing Firestar bathed in a sunspot looking out on other cats of the Clans within a shadowy forest. The series is slated for release in 2028, giving longtime fans the hope they’ve been waiting for all these years.

Virginia (she/her) is IGN’s News Editor. With ten years of experience reporting on games and entertainment, she’s got a storied background in the fighting game community, influencer news, and viral online trends. Find her on Twitter at @TheeMissGlaze.
